title: DPAR: High-Performance, Secure, and Scalable Differential Privacy-based AllReduce
problem: Secure and efficient AllReduce-based data aggregation for distributed HPC/AI workloads requires privacy guarantees while maintaining performance and scalability. Existing Homomorphic Encryption (HE)-based solutions introduce high overhead, demand secure key exchanges, and remain vulnerable to collusion attacks.
motivation: AllReduce is increasingly critical in distributed AI and scientific computing, but privacy concerns have grown. Current SOTA HE-based solutions are expensive and vulnerable to collusion, limiting adoption in large-scale HPC infrastructure.
method: DPAR integrates Differential Privacy (DP) into AllReduce framework with three key components: (1) DP integration to eliminate collusion risks without key exchange, (2) scalable noise growth mechanism to preserve accuracy across aggregation, (3) noise pooling performance optimization. Implemented as MPI AllReduce drop-in replacement.
key_novelty: First differentially private AllReduce framework with collusion resistance that avoids key exchange overhead. Novel noise pooling mechanism enables strong privacy with minimal performance cost.
contributions: First DP-based collusion-resistant AllReduce for large-scale HPC
Scalable noise growth algorithm preserving accuracy in distributed aggregation
Noise pooling optimization reducing performance overhead
MPI-compatible drop-in replacement enabling easy adoption

metrics.speedup: 34.7% faster than SOTA HE solution on modern AI workloads
metrics.privacy: Differential privacy with epsilon-delta guarantees (epsilon/delta parameters implied)

limitations: Abstract only: privacy/accuracy trade-off details not fully specified
Noise growth behavior and epsilon-delta parameters not quantified in abstract
Evaluation limited to modern AI workloads on specific supercomputers
Overhead of DP integration not fully characterized
